title: A runner session hands an item over mid-stage, and the target machine resumes it from the checkpoint

story.as_a: the loop moving an item from minis to x1
story.i_want_to: have minis's runner stop the session, checkpoint its worktree and release, and x1's runner create a worktree at the checkpoint's head with its diff applied before the session starts
story.so_that: an item moves between machines at any stage without a premature commit and without anyone rebuilding its state

rationale: PRD R3: the target 'pulls, creating its own worktree from the item's head plus the shipped diff', and section 8 assigns 'an item moved between machines mid-stage' to this release's end-to-end paths. Today a runner only creates a fresh worktree from the base (LoopctlRunner.Worktree.create/4, /home/mkreyman/workspace/loopctl-runner/lib/loopctl_runner/worktree.ex:586; runner/ after release 2), and a dispatch cannot carry a diff: the runner socket's frames are capped at 64,000 bytes (lib/loopctl_web/endpoint.ex:73). US-52.43 reserves the item for its target; this story is the runner's side and the placement onto the target host.

acceptance_criteria.description: Moves.place_pending/2 runs after a released host-targeted move commits and on every MoveDeadlineWorker pass, and places the item on the target host's runner through Placement.place/4 when that runner is connected, declares the contract version with resume, and has a free slot; otherwise it leaves the reservation for the next pass with no claim and no attempt spent. A move whose target is a holder of kind runner_session is refused 422 code holder_cannot_pull.

Runner contract 1.38.0 (after release 6's 1.37.0, US-52.38): an implement dispatch for a moved item carries resume {move_id, checkpoint_id, branch, head_sha, diff_bytes, diff_sha256, wip_branch, fenced_checkpoint_ids}; control may push move_requested {dispatch_id, claim_epoch, move_id, release_deadline_at}; runner messages checkpoint and checkpoint_fetch are added; session_ended gains reasons moved {move_id, checkpoint_id} and resume_failed {detail}.

RunnerChannel assembles checkpoint parts (each at most 32,768 raw bytes, base64) per dispatch in the channel process, one checkpoint at a time and at most Checkpoints.max_diff_bytes/0 in total, and on the last part records it through Checkpoints.record/4 as the dispatch's runner_session holder at the presented epoch, so a stale epoch takes the fenced path and a resent checkpoint id answers replayed.

RunnerChannel answers checkpoint_fetch {dispatch_id, claim_epoch, checkpoint_id, part} with that part of the diff, parts and diff_sha256 only when the checkpoint belongs to the dispatch's story and the epoch is the dispatch's current one; otherwise stale_claim_epoch or not_found.

On move_requested the runner stops the session through its process group as a wall-clock stop does, records a checkpoint of the worktree (diff against the branch's pushed head, or the base when never pushed) over checkpoint parts, and sends session_ended reason moved with the move_id and checkpoint id, which control applies as the holder's own move release; a diff over the bound is committed to wip/<branch>-e<claim_epoch>, pushed, and checkpointed with wip_branch.

On a dispatch with resume the runner fetches every part, checks diff_sha256, fetches head_sha, creates the worktree on branch at head_sha, applies the diff with `git apply --binary` (for wip_branch, the diff from head_sha to the WIP branch's head), lists fenced_checkpoint_ids in the session's prompt, and only then starts the session; any failure ends the dispatch session_ended resume_failed, which control applies as a counted release that clears pending_move and appends move_resume_failed.

e2e/ path 'an item moved between machines mid-stage', run against loopctl.com and read only through the API and GitHub: on mkreyman/loopctl-e2e-sandbox an item placed on runner A (one of the two fleet runners US-52.9 enrols for the sandbox, named in e2e/config/sandbox.exs) reaches implementing with one uncommitted file, work_item_move to the other runner's host B is called, and the test asserts that the item's newest checkpoint holds that file, that B's session pushes a commit on the item's branch descending from the checkpoint's head_sha and containing the file, that work_item_timeline reads moved then move_pulled with no stage transition by A's holder after moved, and that the item reaches done.

test_cases.name: placement onto the target host only, and waiting when it is full (DataCase)
preconditions: released move to host x1; runners minis and x1 connected through the Presence fixture; x1 at max_sessions in_flight
steps: free a slot on x1; run it again
move a second item to a runner_session holder
expected_results: no claim and attempts unchanged; then claimed on x1 only; 422 holder_cannot_pull

test_cases.name: contract shape and the previous version (unit)
steps: cast a 1.37.0 join and ask Moves.place_pending for that runner
expected_results: resume fields validated; the previous-version runner is skipped, not refused

test_cases.name: checkpoint parts in and out over the socket (channel test)
preconditions: joined RunnerChannel (test/loopctl_web/runner_channel_test.exs) with an accepted dispatch and its holder (US-52.15); a 70,000-byte diff
steps: push one part at the old epoch after a reclaim
fetch from a second dispatch of another story
expected_results: one row recorded; replayed; fenced row; part 1 bytes with parts 3; not_found

test_cases.name: the runner hands over on move_requested (runner unit)
preconditions: runner/ Control test harness with a fake socket and a temp repo whose branch is pushed plus one edit; a stub session process
steps: repeat with a diff over the bound
expected_results: session process group terminated; checkpoint parts sent with the edit; session_ended moved; second case a push of wip/<branch>-e<n> and a checkpoint with wip_branch

test_cases.name: the runner resumes from a checkpoint, and fails cleanly (runner unit)
preconditions: fake socket answering checkpoint_fetch from a fixture diff; temp origin holding head_sha
steps: deliver one whose diff does not apply
expected_results: worktree at head_sha on branch with the edit present before the stub session starts; second: session_ended resume_failed carrying git's message and no session started

test_cases.name: control applies moved and resume_failed (channel test)
preconditions: requested move on an item held by the channel's dispatch; DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
steps: place again and push session_ended resume_failed
expected_results: pending_move released at the checkpoint; then attempts + 1, pending_move nil, one move_resume_failed event

test_cases.name: e2e: an item moved between machines mid-stage
preconditions: mix e2e against loopctl.com with the sandbox's two fleet runners A and B (US-52.9, e2e/config/sandbox.exs) on contract 1.38.0
expected_results: the newest checkpoint holds the uncommitted file, and B pushes a commit descending from its head_sha that contains it
the timeline reads moved then move_pulled, with no transition by A's holder after moved

technical_notes: Placement: Placement.place/4 (lib/loopctl/delivery/placement.ex:372) with the target runner's id; it mints the runner_session holder whose host is the runner's name (US-52.15 AC-52.15.1), which is the caller US-52.43's reservation admits. Selection is not involved: the target is named, and a full or disconnected target waits.

Why the socket and parts: a runner session holds no API credential of its own today (placement.ex:78-94), and the runner socket caps a frame at 64,000 bytes (endpoint.ex:73); parts of 32 KiB fit under the cap after base64. The runner socket is an internal endpoint a machine calls, so it needs no MCP tool (CLAUDE.md, MCP rule exemption).

Server files: RunnerContract (lib/loopctl/api_spec/runner_contract.ex: RunnerDispatch :2421, @version :436, cast_join :3752; a changelog row for 1.38.0), RunnerChannel.handle_in/3 (lib/loopctl_web/runner_channel.ex:335) and the session_ended handling in Loopctl.Delivery.RunnerStages; a counted release is Stages.follow_release/5 with cause :attempt (stages.ex:1659).

Runner files (today in /home/mkreyman/workspace/loopctl-runner, under runner/ after release 2): Control.handle_message/4 'dispatch' (lib/loopctl_runner/control.ex:1509) gains the resume branch and a 'move_requested' clause; the process-group stop is LoopctlRunner.ProcessGroup (process_group.ex); worktree creation reuses Worktree.fetch_commit/4 (worktree.ex:204) and Worktree.create/4 (:586) with head_sha as base; diff capture uses the temporary-index intent-to-add shape US-52.40 measured.

The pushed head the diff is taken against is the remote branch tip after a `git fetch origin <branch>`; when the branch was never pushed, the dispatch's base_branch merge-base. Unpushed commits therefore travel inside the diff.

e2e: the scenario file is e2e/test/move_between_machines_test.exs; the two runners are the fleet runners US-52.9 enrols for the sandbox (e2e/config/sandbox.exs), each on this release's runner; a late report from A after the move is proven by TC-52.44.3's fenced path rather than end to end, because the suite reads no runner's state (README names table: end-to-end suite).
non_goals: An interactive session pulling an item: US-52.46.
Choosing a target host automatically: the caller names it; the loop's own placement by capacity is US-52.47.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.44.3: a runner that loses the socket mid-checkpoint resends every part after reconnecting under the same checkpoint id, and a resend after its claim moved on is stored fenced.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.44.5: the handover state is the checkpoint in loopctl, never the source machine's worktree, so x1 resumes from story_checkpoints even if minis is powered off afterwards.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.44.3: parts are keyed by checkpoint id and a recorded id answers replayed; session_ended is applied once per dispatch as today.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.44.4: a slow link transfers the diff in bounded parts, each its own request, so slowness delays the resume and never corrupts it (diff_sha256 is checked before apply).
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.44.1: the target is reached through its runner's socket by name; the source is reached through its dispatch's socket; neither needs the other's address.

defaults: A resume failure counts as an attempt, so the retry ceiling ends a diff that never applies.
definition_of_done: mix e2e runs move_between_machines_test.exs green against the sandbox repo, and the run's item timeline shows moved, move_pulled and done in that order.
